Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) Appeal If you are notified that you have not met the Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) requirement to continue receiving financial aid, there is an appeal process available if you were prevented from meeting the requirement due to extenuating circumstances.
Students who have been notified, by the AU Office of Student Financial Aid, that they have not met SAP have the option to appeal their aid ineligibility.

All SAP appeals need to be supported by an official third-party individual such as a physician, therapist, counselor, clergy member, law enforcement, or court official that is on official letterhead and signed by said individual.
Once you have added the appeal, a tab should be listed on your account with a SAP Appeal for the aid year.

evidence.snippet: Federal law allows financial aid administrators the authority to exercise professional judgment to adjust the information on the FAFSA on a case-by-case basis for students with special circumstances.

Professional Judgements/Special Circumstance Categories Professional Judgment: Unusual Circumstance Appeal (Dependency Override Appeal) The Dependency Status Override appeal is applicable to students who are otherwise considered dependent students as per federal criteria but were unable to provide parental information.

Professional Judgment: Special Circumstance - SAI Appeal (Income Adjustment Appeal) An Income Adjustment appeal is considered when the income information reported on the FAFSA no longer accurately reflects the student’s and/or family’s ability to contribute toward the student’s education because there are significant changes in income for the student and/or parents (if dependent).

Professional Judgment: Special Circumstance - COA Appeal (Expense Adjustment Appeal) Adjustments to FAFSA data elements or adjustments to a student’s Cost of Attendance (COA) may be made to reflect unusual expenses that directly affect the student’s education.

evidence.snippet: On this page you will find: What is a Professional Judgment?

Types of Circumstances Provisional Independent/ Homeless Youth Determination Homeless Youth Determination Circumstances not considered for PJ Adjustments Regulations and Guidelines Processing Time How to Submit a Professional Judgement (PJ) Request What is a Professional Judgment?

Professional Judgment (PJ) is the authority granted to financial aid administrators to make case-by-case adjustments to a student's Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) information or Student Aid Index (SAI) when documented exceptional, special, or unusual circumstances are not accurately reflected in the standard FAFSA application.

Cost of Attendance (COA) Elements Considered During a Professional Judgment Review When reviewing a student's request for a Cost of Attendance (COA) adjustment through Professional Judgment, the Financial Aid Office may consider documented educational expenses that are not already reflected, or are inadequately reflected, in the student's standard COA.

Circumstances not considered for PJ Adjustments While Professional Judgment (PJ) allows financial aid administrators to consider many unique situations, there are **specific circumstances that federal regulations explicitly do not permit as a basis for adjustments.
Please Note: If your circumstances are not listed above, you may still be eligible to submit a Professional Judgment appeal.

Provisional Independent Status Provisional independent status is granted to students who indicate on the FAFSA that they have unusual circumstances that prevent them from contacting their parents or obtaining their information to complete the FAFSA.
If you have questions about whether or not you may be considered for an Unusual Circumstance appeal, reach out to the Office of Financial Aid.

Direct Outreach for Professional Judgment SUNY has established the option for campuses to meet the direct outreach for professional judgment requirement by using the services of the “Re-Enroll to Complete” vendor.

The vendor, Edfinancial, is a federal student loan servicer whose customer service team can answer level 1 and 2 financial aid questions, including those specific to this direct outreach effort and to inform students of the option to apply for professional judgment.
Edfinancial will answer general Title IV questions as well as questions regarding the requirements for the use of federal professional judgment.
Direct Outreach Communications will meet the ARP requirement by providing information regarding professional judgment availability.

Depending upon the original results of the FAFSA and the magnitude of change, completing a special circumstance could result in a positive financial aid impact or no impact at all.
If this family submits a special circumstance along with supporting documentation, it could result in the addition of a Pell Grant to the student’s financial aid package.
On the other hand, since students with a 0 or negative SAI already have the lowest SAI possible, there is no possible benefit and no reason to submit a special circumstance.
In addition, there would be no reason to submit a special circumstance if a parent’s adjusted gross income slightly changed from $500,000 per year to $490,000 per year.

Please review the steps below to see if a 'Special or Unusual Circumstance' appeal is right for you.
We encourage students who may be eligible for a Special or Unusual Circumstance review to submit documentation through the Student Forms Portal.

Gather and upload supporting documentation based on your situation: Special Circumstance for Financial Adjustment: For situations related to a financial loss or having received a one-time payment (job loss, uninsured medical payments, separate/divorce, death of a parent etc.) submit documentation to vertify your claim.

Examples include, but not limited to, copies of 2025 signed tax returns, proof of one-time payment, death certificates, court documentation for separation or divorce etc.) Special Circumstance: Cost of Attendance (COA) Increase: If you have educational expenses that are higher than our estimated costs, submit proof of the expenses, often by receipt as proof of payment.

Unusual Circumstance Request for Independent Status: For students who need to submit documentation to prove their independent status for the FAFSA, upload two 3rd party statements that verify the student's claim for independence.

Department of Education guided flexibility, to re-evaluate your situation for the following reasons: Loss of job or permanent/indefinite reduction of work hours Separation or divorce Personal bankruptcy that occurs during the current financial aid year Death of a member of your immediate family Reduction/loss of child support High non-reimbursed medical expenses Parents took money out of their pen
If you would like to apply for an American Rescue Plan Special Circumstance, please select one of the links below and download the appropriate form.

evidence.snippet: Extenuating Circumstances Based on extraordinary and special circumstances, and in a specific and limited way, the Department of Education gives authority to a school’s financial aid administrator to make adjustments to the data elements on the FAFSA and to override a student’s dependency status.
The changes to the inputs are dictated by the impact of the special circumstances on the family’s income and assets.

The reason for the adjustment must be documented (by a third party if possible) in the student’s file, and it must relate to the special circumstances that differentiate him or her — not to conditions that exist for a whole class of students.
Dependency Override The Student Financial Services Office may do dependency overrides on a case-by-case basis for students with unusual circumstances.

Please keep in mind none of the conditions listed below, singly or in combination, qualify as unusual circumstances meriting a dependency override: Parents refuse to contribute to the student’s education.

Unusual circumstances do include (and may cause any of the above conditions) abandonment by parents, an abusive family environment that threatens the student’s health or safety, or the student being unable to locate his parents.
